requirement: The getting-started documentation MUST explain that the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill.
rationale:
The subject has one obligation: the getting-started documentation MUST explain that the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill.

Two tests in `tests/repository.rs` carry a `{test}` reference to the subject. They check both `README.md` and `md/getting_started.md`.

- `getting_started_documents_symposium_setup_and_skill_migration`:
  - It requires the words "session", "hook" and "`habeas` skill" in each file.
  - It then splits each file into whitespace-normalized paragraphs. It asserts that one single paragraph contains "hook tells", "load the `habeas` skill before starting any work" and "session". That ties the skill-loading instruction to the hook and the session in the same explanatory text.
  - It also asserts the conditional `habeas setup` advice. That goes beyond the subject but does not weaken the check.
- `installation_guides_cover_setup_hooks_refresh_and_preserving_local_skills`:
  - It asserts that both files contain "load the `habeas` skill".
  - It asserts the exact sentences in `README.md` ("Its session-start hook tells the agent that the project tracks requirements with Habeas and to load the `habeas` skill before starting any work.") and in `md/getting_started.md` ("When an agent starts a session in this project, Habeas's hook tells it ... load the `habeas` skill before starting any work.").

Together these assertions would fail if the explanation were removed or reworded to drop the hook directing skill loading. There are no other modes, boundaries or failure cases in the requirement text. The tests are marked and have real assertions, so I found no gap.
